title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.8982: the arrival fused into pass 1 on a 2^24-row table, h = 0.00005, kappa = 1.0001

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.8982 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 4c8222cc (125.9016: 673640ef's kernels, loops and rows with fkiene's doubling recount from 0a1c5772, a partition table of R = 2^24 rows, h = 0.00005, p0 = 0.3900503, and kappa = 1.0001 from its shipped hazard census, all unchanged) with one change: each walk's arrival (key, distinguished and filter tests, 25-bit table address) runs inside the next round's pass 1 (kernels/secp_fuse.s), which forms dx from the x(W) limbs the arrival loaded, so the fused pass 1 is 16,516 instructions per 128 walks, 129.03125 per walk, against 99.515625 + 31.015625 before. The ordinary step is 129.03125 + 444.515625 + 25614/2^20 = 573.5713 instructions; anchor rounds run the unfused arrival and pass 1 and are charged 14 instructions per walk per anchor as a hard row; the doubling is priced as the displaced step plus a whole 677 milli-units, and a doubling walk's displaced addition is charged in the rare-exit row too; true filter hits are charged at twice the doubling rate (a traversal's hit and its closing arrival). Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and a rare-path entry 25, before their tails run; the shipped fused rare path is a logging test stub, and the production rare path is specified and priced in proof.md section 2.5. The declared run executes the shipped loops, the fused pass 1 and the arrival rows at exactly these counts, enters all 1,167 exit stubs of the unfused loops and, in the fused pass 1, forces each rare kind, fe_sub exits (one in walk 0) and product carries (548 walks, 79 rare entries, 40 exits, 0 mismatches). Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): 4c8222cc, 0a1c5772, 673640ef, 6a6cb91c, 610c8e49, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 2bd168b5, 01488655, daf2c741, 4b4defe7, b78fb4f6, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, 2d25756c, b5de673a, 13c3295f, f99114e0, 02feb284. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995074, phase 1 = 2^125.897553, hard extras = 2^112.763609, random extras = 2^99.7836, allowance = 2^114.0713, W_ledger = 2^125.8981099 < 2^125.8982; Markov ratio 0.0000407504 (experiment.py's float ledger: 0.0000407522) < 0.00005; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1258982 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1258981 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
